name_note: GTDB places this species in the split genus Alistipes_A, so its GTDB genus is narrower than the classical genus Alistipes used in the literature cited here.

sentences.text: Alistipes indistinctus is an anaerobic, non-spore-forming, non-motile, Gram-negative-staining bacterium of the family Rikenellaceae, named from strains isolated from human faeces.
A review states that Alistipes species are typically isolated from the human gut microbiome and that evidence on their effects is contrasting, with both protective and harmful associations reported.
A study reported that the abundance and centrality of Alistipes indistinctus are depleted in subjects with hyperuricemia, and identified hippuric acid as the microbial effector lowering uric acid.
A dietary intervention study reported increased relative abundance of Alistipes indistinctus after restriction of advanced glycation end products.
